2. The petitioner would submit that he is the owner of the land comprised in S.No.716/2 measuring an extent of 5 acres in Adhagapadi Village, Dharmapuri Taluk and Dharmapuri District.

3. The Petitioner would submit that the Government of Tamil Nadu had issued a G.O.Ms.No.284 Industries (SIPCOT-L.A) Department dated 30.12.2015 and accorded administrative sanction for acquisition of 222.81 hectares of Patta lands under the provisions of the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of L a n d f o r I n d u s t r i a l P u r p o s e s A c t , 1 9 9 7 ( h e r e i n a f t e r c a l l e d a s t h e " A c t " )

4. The petitioner would submit that on 13.11.2016 the District Collector had issued a notification in Daily Thanthi and Trinity Mirror Newspaper Daily U/s.3(2) AA of the Act.
The District Collector had also issued a notice U/s. 3(2) A of the Act to him.
On 03.12.2016, the petitioner had submitted his detailed objections to the District Collector.
However, without considering the objections, the 5th respondent /District Collector mechanically rejected the representation on 08.03.2017.

Thereafter,
the 5th Respondent had proceeded with the proposal under Section 3(1) of the Act and drafted costs for acquiring the industry lands.

5. The petitioner would submit that thereafter based on the Valuation Sub-Committee order of reducing the guideline value in respect of the Survey Numbers pertaining to Land acquisition, the land Acquisition Officers/ the 7th Respondent requested the 6th Respondent / The District Registrar, Dharmapuri in Na.Ka.No.147/2016/A2 dated 28.11.2018 to revise the guideline value in so far as the acquisition of land survey https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
03/03/2025 04:35:28 pm ) numbers are concerned and thereafter the District Collector/ 5th respondent based on the Valuation Sub-Committee Proceedings/order, passed the Compensation award/Decree in Na.Ka.No.30/2016/ Unit 1 in respect of BLOCK No:9 without considering the detailed objections of the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court.

6. Heard the counsels on either side and perused the records.
7.
It is seen that without considering the detailed objections of the petitioner dated 03.12.2016, the impugned award has been passed by the 5th respondent as early as in the year 2021.
As per Section 8 of the Act, the application for reference had to be made within a period of 60 days.
However, the petitioner has approached the Court only now.

8. Therefore, in the light of the above above judgement, the State having received the objections of the petitioner ought to have made the reference in time.

Therefore, this Writ Petition is disposed of directing the 5th respondent to refer the matter to the competent Civil Court as per Section 8 of the Act within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
